channel.title: Btwinus Blog
channel.description: Practical writing on private messaging, end-to-end encryption, anonymous chat, and how to share secrets safely without leaving a trail.

item.title: How to share a password without leaving a copy behind
item.description: Email, Slack, and WhatsApp keep a copy of every password you send. Here's what actually goes wrong, and the safer ways to share credentials.

item.title: Encrypted chat with no account: how Btwinus puts AES-256 in a link
item.description: Most 'encrypted' messengers still need a phone number and a server. Here's how Btwinus puts real AES-256 directly inside a shareable link.

item.title: Signal vs Telegram vs Btwinus: which one is actually anonymous?
item.description: The word 'anonymous' gets thrown around loosely in messaging. Here's how Signal, Telegram, and Btwinus actually compare on identity, server retention, and metadata leakage — with an honest table.

item.title: For journalists: how to receive anonymous tips without leaving a server trail
item.description: Most 'secure' tip lines still leak metadata or require sources to install something. Here's a practical guide to receiving anonymous tips with the lowest possible friction and the smallest possible trail.
